The phrasing of your question ("alarm going off during a 'deep dream'") indicates to me that you aren't quite aware of sleep cycles and how they work.

There are four stages of sleep: alpha, beta, delta, and REM which are named for the waves that your brain emits during these stages and for Rapid Eye Movement (which you probably knew). You pass through each of these stages 4-6 times in a night, where alpha, beta and REM are the lightest and delta is the deepest, most restorative sleep. [I think REM actually occurs when your brain is in beta/alpha and that they aren't distinct from a brainwave standpoint, but I need to double check on that.] During REM, your brain is essentially awake/active, though your body is likely in sleep paralysis to keep you from acting on your dream states. As the night progresses, you spend more and more time in REM and less in delta, which is why you dream more towards the morning than when you first go to sleep.

Dreaming only occurs during REM and the lightest part of your cycle after your brain has moved out of deep sleep. in fact, many people do wake up during each alpha but just don't remember because they immediately/subconciously fall back to sleep. I used to stress that I was waking up all the time in the middle of the night, but now that I know that's normal and natural, it doesn't bother me and I "feel" like I'm getting better quality sleep, when it's probably more likely that I'm getting the same quality but my attitude has just changed.

If you're feeling groggy when you wake up, I would try to time your sleep cycles better by using the website http://sleepyti.me to try to wake up in alpha rather than beta. From my previously example, I've found it's more about the mindset and the knowledge of how sleep works that dictates how I "feel" in the morning. Anyway, you typically only remember dreams when you interrupt them by waking up, but we have 4-6 distinct dreams every night, one during each cycle.
